Soil heat flux of the reference surface

Source: R/reference-et.R
ef_ref_soil_heat_flux.Rd

Computes the soil heat flux \(G\) of the hypothetical reference surface from its net radiation, with the ratios of the reference evapotranspiration standards: zero for daily periods, and a fixed fraction of the net radiation, different by day and by night, for hourly periods. It is the soil heat flux entering ef_ref_et(); it is not a method for the soil heat flux of a pixel (ef_g()).

Usage

ef_ref_soil_heat_flux(
  net_radiation,
  reference,
  timestep,
  standard,
  daytime = NULL
)

Arguments

net_radiation

Numeric. Net radiation of the reference surface \(R_n\) [MJ m-2 d-1 or MJ m-2 h-1], for example ef_ref_net_radiation()$rn. Any finite value.

reference

Character, no default. Reference crop: "grass" (short reference, 0.12 m) or "alfalfa" (tall reference, about 0.5 m).

timestep

Character, no default. "daily" or "hourly".

standard

Character, no default. "fao56" (FAO-56, grass only) or "asce" (ASCE-EWRI 2005 standardized equation).

daytime

Logical or NULL. For timestep = "hourly", TRUE for daytime and FALSE for night-time periods (required); must be NULL for "daily". NA gives NA. The criterion is the caller's choice (decision WF-15): FAO-56 speaks of "daylight periods" without a threshold; ASCE-EWRI (2005) defines daytime as a positive hourly net radiation, daytime = net_radiation > 0 (see Details).

Value

A numeric vector of soil heat flux of the reference surface \(G\) in the unit of net_radiation, with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim. For daily periods it is 0 (and NA where net_radiation is NA).

Details

\(G = c_G R_n\) with \(c_G\) from the internal constants table of the reference equations (dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 5.3):

Reference, standardDailyHourly, dayHourly, nightStatus
grass, "fao56"0 (Eq. 42)0.1 (Eq. 45)0.5 (Eq. 46)VERIFICADA
grass, "asce"0 (Eq. 30)0.1 (Eq. 65a)0.5 (Eq. 65b)VERIFICADA
alfalfa, "asce"0 (Eq. 30)0.04 (Eq. 66a)0.2 (Eq. 66b)VERIFICADA

FAO-56 (Eq. 42) and ASCE-EWRI (2005, Eq. 30, p. 25) state that the daily soil heat flux beneath the reference surface is small and is ignored (G = 0). The monthly forms (FAO-56 Eqs. 43-44; ASCE-EWRI Eqs. 31-32) are out of scope.

Day and night in ASCE-EWRI (2005). The report defines daytime as a positive mean net radiation of the hourly period (text before Table 1, p. 5; Table 2, p. 5: daytime \(R_n > 0\), night-time \(R_n \le 0\)), which daytime = net_radiation > 0 follows (option "rn_positive" of ef_station_ref_et()). The report is not consistent at \(R_n = 0\): p. 44 (after Eqs. 65-66) and the glossary (p. 58) define night-time as \(R_n < 0\) and daytime as \(R_n \ge 0\). At \(R_n = 0\) G is 0 under both readings; only \(C_d\) of ef_ref_et() depends on it.

standard = "fao56" with reference = "alfalfa" raises earthflux_undefined_reference (also earthflux_input_error): FAO-56 does not define the tall reference.

Missing values propagate. Missing or unknown choices raise earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method; a missing or non-logical daytime where required, or a daytime given for a daily step, raise earthflux_input_error (or earthflux_missing_input); infinite net_radiation raises earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

FAO-56 grass rows: VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 4, Eqs. 42, 45, 46; cases V15 and V16). ASCE-EWRI rows: VERIFICADA (ASCE-EWRI, 2005, Eq. 30, p. 25; Eqs. 65a-b and 66a-b, p. 44).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other reference evapotranspiration functions: ef_ref_et(), ef_ref_net_radiation(), ef_station_ref_et()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 19: daytime (Rn = 1.749) and night (Rn = -0.100) hours
ef_ref_soil_heat_flux(c(1.749, -0.100), reference = "grass",
                      timestep = "hourly", standard = "fao56",
                      daytime = c(TRUE, FALSE))
#> [1]  0.1749 -0.0500

# Tall reference, ASCE-EWRI daytime rule (Rn > 0)
rn <- c(1.749, -0.100)
ef_ref_soil_heat_flux(rn, reference = "alfalfa", timestep = "hourly",
                      standard = "asce", daytime = rn > 0)
#> [1]  0.06996 -0.02000

# Daily step: G = 0
ef_ref_soil_heat_flux(13.28, reference = "grass", timestep = "daily",
                      standard = "fao56")
#> [1] 0
